lanes.title: battalions: DR24's sizes, the battalion as the command unit, 25 per army, at most 5 per side in a battle, healing (D-087 DF12, D-088 DG3-DG6, D-090 DI2)
lanes.brief:
SCOPE LIMITS: as lane OC: prototypes/m7-sprint1 (M7Proto.slnx; M7Econ.slnx where war economics is touched) and docs/m7-plan only; no Sim.* change, no permanent project, no CI change. PROPOSAL where the Director delegated; READING with both alternatives; nothing invented or reopened.

READ FIRST: D-087 (DF12, DF12-R1, §4 on lane CB, §6), D-088 (DG3 with DG3-R1 and DG3-R2, DG4, DG5 with DG5-R1 to DG5-R3, DG6, §0 item 3's ADMIN note, §5), D-089 DH9 and D-090 (DI2, DI2-R1); D-079 DR23 to DR25 (DR24 sets the size of ONE FORMATION, not a per-army cap), D-082 DA3 and DA5; docs/m7-plan/caps-and-counted-objects-proposal.md (§2: DR24's table and the counted objects), battle-entity-proposal.md, unit-catalogue-and-progression.md (the unit types; §4.5's A-E classification) and economic-scale-proposal.md; reports H-OC (the outcome rules you build on), H-CB, H-D (the caps prototype, the War Sandbox), H-N (the battle-entry table), H-E (war economics), H-S (garrisons), H-W; code Proto.M7/Caps, Proto.M7/Tactical (FormationSpec, BattleSetup, PersonnelLedger), Proto.M7/Sandbox, Proto.M7/War (ActionWindows' action points, Concealment's EngagementBattle) and Proto.M7/WarEcon.

(1) BATTALION SIZES (D-090 DI2; DI2-R1). One table, one source of truth: a battalion size for every unit type in the unit catalogue. DR24's values wherever DR24 sets one: heavy or aggregated infantry 50, archers or light infantry 60, tanks 5, helicopters 3, ships 5, fixed-wing aircraft 1, snipers 2, mortars 5, each counted as caps proposal §2 counts it (battle entities, vehicles, helicopters, hulls, airframes, crewed tubes). For every type DR24 does not size (lane CB's CAP-5 families: cavalry, siege, air defence, missiles, reconnaissance; and any other catalogue type), a PROPOSED size in DR24's spirit with its reasoning, for the Director. D-087 DF12's numbers (50 archers, 5 tanks, 2 jets) were examples, not values (DI2). A test pins DR24's values and cites the decision. Classify any new entity A-E first (unit catalogue §4.5).

(2) THE BATTALION AS THE COMMAND UNIT (D-087 DF12; D-088 DG6, confirming DF12-R1 (a)). In battle only a battalion can be ordered to take a formation or to attack; an order to an individual unit is refused with a stable code. Inside a battalion each tank, jet or group of soldiers stays its own battle entity (lane CB's entity rule is kept). Both resolvers and the War Sandbox take battalion orders; a battalion below full strength fights with what it has. Turn-exact pins for when a battalion order applies relative to when it was issued; tests.

(3) THE ARMY CAP (D-087 DF12; D-082 DA5 narrowed). An army holds at most 25 battalions: the caps prototype counts battalions and refuses a 26th with a stable code, and the War Sandbox applies the cap (DA5: caps apply in the sandbox). DR24's sizes are battalion sizes, not per-army caps. D-088 DG4: DR25's '50,000 troops difficult' is an empire's total across its armies, and battalions stay small. MEASURE and tabulate what 25 battalions of each type hold (persons, machines) and how many armies an empire needs for 50,000 troops, at each stage (D-082 DA3).

(4) AT MOST 5 BATTALIONS PER SIDE IN A BATTLE (D-088 DG3; DG3-R1 (a), applied: 5 in total per side, of every kind). The side's own empire's battalions come first, and its allies' fill what is left (the Director's example: an attacking player's 4 and its allies' 2 give the player's 4 and one of the allies'; the same for the defending side). DG3-R2, which of the empire's own battalions fight when it alone has more than 5, is a PROPOSAL: for example the player's choice, else a deterministic order by a composite key with a stable integer tie-break, proved by a tie-dense test. Which allied battalion fills a slot when several qualify: likewise. PROPOSE what happens to the battalions not admitted (for example they stay on the map, out of the battle) and state it. Apply the limit wherever a battle is built (EngagementBattle, the War Sandbox, lane OC's ambush battle); tests, including the Director's example and ties.

(5) HEALING (D-088 DG5; DG5-R1 (a), DG5-R2 delegated, DG5-R3 (a); this answers lane CB's READING CB-4). A damaged battalion heals by consuming resources, only while garrisoned or in territory its empire controls; healing takes one full turn and all of that turn's action points. One turn restores the battalion to full strength when its cost is paid in full; a shortfall restores it in proportion to what was paid. What it consumes (DG5-R2, PROPOSAL): recruits, that is people moved through the ledger (Law 1: Ledger.Transfer only, long stocks, exact-equality tests), and the equipment or money its type needs (lane E's war economics). Refusals with stable codes (not garrisoned and outside its territory; action points already spent; nothing to pay with). Turn-exact pins (the heal completes at the end of the turn it occupies); conservation tests with exact equality.

(6) DOCUMENTS AND CHECKS. A design document, docs/m7-plan/battalion-proposal.md (DR24's values cited as decided; PROPOSAL where design); dated in-place notes where caps-and-counted-objects-proposal.md, battle-entity-proposal.md or the unit catalogue are superseded or narrowed; a populated-table round-trip test for every new serialized row (exact ExpectedLength, bit-exact round-trip, hash equality); a semantic test per mechanism; bounded mutants with semantic kills; lane P's battery re-measured if outputs change; the determinism scan; the doc-link check. The report states the battalion model that lane AR must auto-resolve.
